confirmed: Source is the 2025 Cambridge journal version of record, 17 PDF pages, with matching authors; the complete markdown was read through the references. Supplementary Materials S1–S3 are separate examples of high/low ratings and were not read (p. 1, publication details; p. 9, Idea assessment results; p. 15, Supplementary material).

Study 1 is a preliminary survey, not an AI-assistance experiment: 64 industrial-design master students with prior ChatGPT ideation experience; Table 1 uses 64 respondents for every item (pp. 3-4, Protocol/Results of study 1; Table 1).

Study 2 explicitly randomly divides 48 people into six task/assistance cells, with eight per cell; 24 assigned per assistance arm is the transparent sum 8+8+8 from Table 2 (p. 8, Participants, Design study and Table 2).

The reported controlled design session supports lab_rct, individual assignment and between-person structure. Participants generated at least four ideas individually in 30 minutes for a trash can, alarm or kitchen blender; each submission had a title and approximately 40 words, and sketches were not analyzed (p. 8, Design study; Tables 2-3).

Treatment used Co-Ideator powered by ChatGPT 4.0 as named in the protocol, with free interaction after the initial prompt and optional prompts requesting suggestions, alternative solutions and final ideas; control received no additional help (p. 8, Design study; p. 9, Table 4).
Figures 11 and 12 visibly show 24 responses in each post-task survey; these are survey denominators (p. 13, Figure 11; p. 14, Figure 12; also p. 12, novelty Discussion).
Novelty: treatment mean rank 110.28 versus control 93.64, U=4306.5, Z=−2.051, p=0.040 (p. 10, novelty Results; p. 11, Discussion).
Quality/feasibility: treatment mean rank 126.80 versus control 76.96, U=2621.5, Z=−6.278, p<0.001 (p. 10, quality Results; p. 11, Discussion).

Variety: treatment mean rank 107.80 versus control 96.14, U=4559.5, Z=−1.500, p=0.133; this is within-person flexibility, not across-person homogenization (p. 9, definition; p. 10, variety Results; p. 11, Discussion; p. 13, variety Discussion).

The form correctly flags the Figure 8 caption’s conflicting novelty/quality labels and the quality paragraph’s stray word novelty; the Results and Discussion consistently support the one-line finding (pp. 10-11, Results, Figure 8 caption and Discussion).

Core=no, random-assignment criterion=met, output-scored-outcome criterion=met, sample-size criterion=not_met, and context_class=none are appropriate: even the randomized sample is below 50 people, and the preliminary survey cannot increase that experimental sample (p. 8, assignment; p. 9, scoring; codebook sections 3-4).
This is a primary empirical paper, not a synthesis; no pooled estimates or standardized pooled effects are reported (pp. 3-4, Study 1; pp. 7-14, Study 2 and Discussion).
summary: Study 2 randomly assigned 48 people to Co-Ideator or no AI and scored their ideas, so it belongs in the two-screener pipeline but remains below the core sample threshold. The main finding is supported, but corrections are needed for unconfirmed analyzed-person counts, conflicting idea totals, an omitted quantity outcome, incomplete outcome fields, and corrupted punctuation and minus signs.
